info.name: hl-api
info.description:
Test collection for hl-api.

Set `baseUrl` (default http://localhost:8080).

SCOPE: this API is called by our own mobile app and by our own scheduled jobs. It is not a public API. Every endpoint has one of those two callers; anything without one was deleted.

WORKS WITH NO CREDENTIALS
- Ops: healthz, readyz (metrics needs METRICS_TOKEN)
- Public reads: earnings calendar + per-ticker earnings detail
  (these need Supabase creds on the SERVER, not in Postman)

NEEDS A PRIVY ACCESS TOKEN
Everything else. Paste one into `privyToken`.

Postman CANNOT mint that token: Privy access tokens are ES256 JWTs signed with Privy's private key, issued only through a real sign-in in the SDK. Get one by signing in on the iOS app and reading privy.user.getAccessToken().

TRADES NEED MORE THAN A TOKEN
They verify against Hyperliquid by client order id, so they need a real filled order whose cloid you know. A valid token alone returns 409 fill_not_found. The iOS app attaches one to every order it reports.

item.name: Ops
item.description: Liveness and readiness need no credentials; metrics needs METRICS_TOKEN.

request.description: 200 {"status":"ok"} if the process is up.
200 when Supabase is reachable; reports auth-bridge state.
Prometheus exposition format. Needs the server's METRICS_TOKEN in `metricsToken`; 404 when the server has none set.

item.name: Public reads (no auth)
item.description: Anonymous. These need Supabase credentials on the SERVER, not in Postman — they work as soon as hl-api is running.

request.description: Upcoming earnings calendar, shaped 1:1 to the app's MarketEvent. Supabase-only; no price data.

ANONYMOUS. One ticker's next earnings event, past results and beat odds — the asset page's earnings section.

Use AAPL, MSFT, IBM or INTC. Those are the only tickers the current Benzinga plan entitles, so everything else returns nulls and empty arrays. That is a data-coverage limit, not a bug.

Accepts numeric tickers (XYZ100, SP500, JP225, KR200, H100), which the old /v1/assets/:ticker rejected.

item.name: Identity (auth)
item.description: Sign-up, profile and usernames. Needs a Privy access token in `privyToken`.

request.description:
AUTHENTICATED. Idempotent - call on every launch. Verifies the Privy token, resolves and stores the embedded wallet, creates the profile, and mints a Supabase session JWT.

201 on first call, 200 after. Read `walletStatus`:
- resolved        -> wallet stored
- unresolved      -> Privy hasn't provisioned it yet; retry
- not_configured  -> PRIVY_APP_SECRET missing on this deployment

`needsUsername: true` means onboarding isn't finished. Copy `supabaseAccessToken` into the `supabaseToken` variable for direct Supabase calls.
Verified id + wallet; lazily upserts the profile row. 503 until Privy wired; 401 without a token.
AUTHENTICATED. A HINT only - racy by construction, so a green answer here can still lose a race at claim time. Checks the all-time namespace, so a name someone else released stays unavailable.

AUTHENTICATED. Atomic - the unique index decides a race.

409 username_taken is a NORMAL outcome, not an error.
400 for a rule violation (3-20 chars, [a-z0-9_], must start with a letter, not reserved).

The username is also the referral code, so a released name is never reassigned - only its original owner can reclaim it.

AUTHENTICATED. Raw image bytes, not multipart. Pick a file under Body > binary and set Content-Type to match: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/heic or image/heif. Max 12 MB.

Re-encoded to a 512px square WebP (which strips EXIF/GPS) and stored in the public avatars bucket. Returns the updated profile.

400 if the bytes are not a readable image, or if no profile exists yet (call signup first).
AUTHENTICATED. Idempotent. Clears the photo; the app falls back to its drawn default. Returns the updated profile.

item.name: Trades & takes (auth)
item.description: Needs a Privy token AND a real filled Hyperliquid order whose cloid you know — these verify against the exchange, so a valid token alone returns 409 fill_not_found.

request.description:
AUTHENTICATED. Call AFTER submitting an order to Hyperliquid.

Verifies the fill by client order id and records the position. Side, size and price come from HL's fills, never from this body - so a real filled order with a cloid is required.

409 fill_not_found is also the correct answer for an IOC that never filled: treat it as 'no position, no composer', not a retry loop.
409 flip_unsupported for a position flip.

PREREQUISITE: the app must attach a cloid. HLClient.orderAction supports it (the `c` field) but placeOrder passes nil today.

AUTHENTICATED. Stamps exit price and realized PnL onto the open position and opens a second take window.

409 no_open_position when nothing matching is on file - e.g. the position was opened outside the app.

AUTHENTICATED. Optional - the trade is recorded either way.

The cloid says which trade, and therefore whether this is the opening or closing take.

Normal refusals:
- 409 already_posted  -> one take per trade
- 403 not_yours / 404 unknown_trade

Posting is the consent moment: the position only becomes publicly readable once it carries a take.

item.name: Feed (auth)
item.description: Reading the position feed — the counterpart to POST /v1/takes. Only positions carrying a take appear, since posting is what publishes a position.

request.description:
AUTHENTICATED. Newest trade first.

`?coin=TSLA` for one room, `?user=<did>` for one author's history, neither for everything.

A position with both an open and a close take appears as TWO items — they are two posts made at different times. The close one carries realizedPnl and the exit price.

AUTHENTICATED. Long/short split for a room.

Counts every position opened through the app on this coin, open or closed, with or without a take. `basis: app_positions` says so in the response. Positions opened outside the app aren't on file.
AUTHENTICATED. The caller's starred tickers, newest first. Private — no one else can read it, not even with the anon key.

AUTHENTICATED. Idempotent — 200 either way, `added` says whether this call changed anything. Not 409 on a repeat, since the client toggles optimistically.

Accepts numeric tickers (XYZ100, SP500). Not validated against the assets catalogue, which is sparser than the live HL universe.
AUTHENTICATED. Idempotent — `removed` says whether anything changed.

item.name: Notifications (auth)
item.description:
Device registration, the inbox, and push preferences.

DORMANT until APNS_KEY / APNS_KEY_ID / APNS_TEAM_ID are set — but not broken: notifications are still written to the server-side inbox, so nothing is lost. `pushConfigured` on the register response says which state you are in.

The app also cannot register yet: it has no AppDelegate, so the APNs device token is never captured. It requests permission and discards the token.

request.description:
AUTHENTICATED. Idempotent — call on every launch; it refreshes last_seen_at and clears a previous invalidation after a reinstall.

`environment` is REQUIRED and cannot be inferred server-side: a token from a debug build only works against APNs sandbox, and a production server legitimately serves TestFlight builds too. Getting it wrong returns BadDeviceToken and invalidates the token.
AUTHENTICATED. For sign-out. Deletes rather than invalidates — this is the user's own choice, not APNs telling us the token is dead, and the distinction is worth keeping.

AUTHENTICATED. Newest first, with an `unread` count for the badge. `?limit= &offset=`

Server-side rather than the app's UserDefaults, so it survives a reinstall, matches across devices, and still shows a message whose push failed.
AUTHENTICATED. Matches the app's InboxStore.markAllRead() — opening the inbox counts as viewing it, so there is no per-item call.

AUTHENTICATED. Returns defaults when no row exists, so the client never special-cases a user who has not opened settings.

`alwaysDelivered` lists the categories quiet hours never apply to.

AUTHENTICATED. Partial update — send only what changed.

Quiet hours need a `timezone` to mean anything, and a window may wrap midnight (22 -> 7). They apply to informational categories only: a liquidation warning is never held back, which is enforced in code rather than left to this setting.

variable.description: Client order id from a real Hyperliquid order. Required by the trade endpoints.
APNs device token from the app. Hex, 64 chars on current iOS.
